messages:
Anika: Proposal: stop implicit weight-drift fallback and add explicit `fallback_quota` in the policy DSL. Runtime shim preserves legacy policies. Need migration and canary plan.

Ethan: +1 for explicit DSL. Legacy compatibility is key. How will shim be encoded?

Anika: Compiler emits `fallback_quota: {mode: calculated_legacy}` when absent. New policies set `mode: explicit` with `budget_per_min` and `burst`.

Priya: Telemetry change: add `fallback_quota_assigned`, `fallback_quota_consumed`, `fallback_token_evicted_reason`. Hash tenant ids; no prompt text.

Marco: Record probe latency & capacity signal at fallback time so we can correlate.

Devon: Ops note: canary must include hard per-tenant token caps and an emergency router-level kill switch to set `fallback_quota=0`.

Ethan: Runtime approach: sidecar translation is safer for canary (fast rollback). Later convert to compile-time expansion for perf.

Priya: Add compiler tests for deterministic mapping from historical metrics -> `calculated_legacy` values.

Marco: Run simulation against 30-day traces. Fail rollout if cost >15% or p99 latency +50ms.

Devon: Ops checklist: alert thresholds, billing ties, runbook, sales notifications for affected enterprise tenants.

Ethan: Add hook `on_fallback_eval(context) -> token_grant` so quota service can veto. Default no-op.

Anika: Timeline: design doc (week1), implement sidecar+metrics (wks2-3), run simulations (wk4), small canary (wk5), progressive rollout (wk6-8).

ops-bot: Runbook stub created: https://internal/runbooks/fallback-quota | canary-channel: eng-runtime | budget: ops-budget-2028

Anika: I'll draft the RFC and ping for review. If no objections I'll post EOD. :thumbsup:
